newsitem.title: USA: Angelica sees Q3 below expectations.
newsitem.headline: Angelica sees Q3 below expectations.

text.p: Angelica Corp said it expects third-quarter earnings to be below its previous expectations and below year-ago quarter levels.

"In addition, a weak third quarter, which in the past has been Angelica's strongest quarter, will make it unlikely that earnings for the full fiscal year ending on January 25, 1997, will exceed the $1.08 per share (before restructuring charge) earned in the prior fiscal year," the company said.
Shares in the textiles rental and laundry concern closed off 1/4 to 21-5/8 Friday on the New York Stock Exchange.
The company posted third quarter earnings of $2.8 million, or $0.31 per share, on revenues of $123.5 million in the third quarter of the preceding fiscal year.

"Lower than expected revenues combined with an unexpected increase in pressure on prices and margins from the health care markets have adversely affected the textile services segment. Additionally, this segment continues to suffer from operational problems at a few plants," the company said.

"In the manufacturing and marketing segments, lower than expected sales volumes are causing results to be below planned amounts. Sales and earnings gains at Life Retail Stores have moderated from levels seen earlier in the year, but this segment is still on track to post another year of record results," the company said.
In addition to difficulties in the healthcare market, Angelica said cost savings expected to result from a recent restructuring are being realized slower than planned.
"Greater benefits from these consolidations are expected to be realized in the fourth quarter of this year," it said.
Wall Street had expected Angelica to report earnings of aboout $0.35 per share in the third quarter and about $1.25 per share in fiscal 1997, according to First Call.
